name: data_forms_tool
description: Data tool - Read forms and manage form submissions on a site. Actions: list_forms, get_form, list_site_form_submissions, list_form_submissions, get_form_submission, update_form_submission, delete_form_submission.

label.description: Label echoed in the response for this action item. It does not select which action runs.

form_submission_id.description: The form submission ID (ObjectId) to delete.

delete_form_submission.description: Delete a form submission. DESTRUCTIVE and not reversible — confirm with the user before calling.

anyOf.description: Run delete_form_submission: Delete a form submission. DESTRUCTIVE and not reversible — confirm with the user before calling.

get_form.description: Get the schema for a single form, including field definitions and form metadata. Pass form_id (the form's ObjectId, discoverable via list_forms).

anyOf.description: Run get_form: Get the schema for a single form, including field definitions and form metadata. Pass form_id (the form's ObjectId, discoverable via list_forms).

get_form_submission.description: Get a single form submission by ID. Returns the submission's field values and metadata.

anyOf.description: Run get_form_submission: Get a single form submission by ID. Returns the submission's field values and metadata.

limit.description: Maximum number of submissions to return (1-100). Defaults to 25.

list_form_submissions.description: List submissions for a specific form on a site. Pass site_id and form_id (ObjectId). Supports pagination via limit and offset.

anyOf.description: Run list_form_submissions: List submissions for a specific form on a site. Pass site_id and form_id (ObjectId). Supports pagination via limit and offset.

limit.description: Maximum number of forms to return (1-100). Defaults to 25.

list_forms.description: List forms on a site. Returns form metadata (id, displayName, fields, etc.). Supports pagination via limit and offset.

anyOf.description: Run list_forms: List forms on a site. Returns form metadata (id, displayName, fields, etc.). Supports pagination via limit and offset.

element_id.description: Form element GUID to filter submissions to a specific form element. Note: this is the form's element GUID (a plain string), not an ObjectId form_id.

locale_id.description: Locale ID (ObjectId) to filter submissions by locale.

limit.description: Maximum number of submissions to return (1-100). Defaults to 25.

list_site_form_submissions.description: List form submissions across an entire site. Optionally filter by element_id (the form element GUID, NOT a form ObjectId) to scope to a specific form element, or locale_id to scope to a locale. Supports pagination via limit and offset.

anyOf.description: Run list_site_form_submissions: List form submissions across an entire site. Optionally filter by element_id (the form element GUID, NOT a form ObjectId) to scope to a specific form element, or locale_id to scope to a locale. Supports pagination via limit and offset.

form_submission_data.description: Object of field name → value to write to the submission's user-hidden fields. Replaces the values of the listed fields; other fields are untouched.

update_form_submission.description: Update user-hidden field values on a form submission. Pass site_id, form_submission_id, and form_submission_data (an object mapping field name → value). Only user-hidden fields are writable.

anyOf.description: Run update_form_submission: Update user-hidden field values on a form submission. Pass site_id, form_submission_id, and form_submission_data (an object mapping field name → value). Only user-hidden fields are writable.

actions.description: Actions to execute sequentially. Each array item must include label and exactly one action property: delete_form_submission, get_form, get_form_submission, list_form_submissions, list_forms, list_site_form_submissions, update_form_submission.

context.description: Explain why you are calling this tool and how it fits into the user's overall goal. This parameter is used for analytics and user intent tracking. YOU MUST provide 15-25 words (count carefully). NEVER use first person ('I', 'we', 'you') - maintain third-person perspective. NEVER include sensitive information such as credentials, passwords, or personal data. Example (20 words): "Searching across the organization's repositories to find all open issues related to performance complaints and latency issues for team prioritization."
